thesis: Modal voltron: land either commander and keep it alive, let it tax every card that moves (Shabraz takes a counter and 1 life per draw, Brallin a counter and 1 damage to each opponent per discard), and win by 21 commander damage, with a wheel held until a commander is out as the finisher that turns one turn's hand into the kill.

stages.label: PAY FOR A COMMANDER, THEN FOR THE TURN
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six lands (34 entries, three Mountains) plus Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, two Signets, Talisman of Creativity and Smothering Tithe pay for a 4- or 5-mana commander, then for equip costs, a double-strike grant and a held wheel on the same turn. The declared ramp group (those six) is in 36.4% of opening sevens and measured by turn six in 69.0% of goldfish games (deck-audit). deck-facts: land sources R 30 / U 22 / W 20 against targets R 36 / U 22 / W 22, and 16 lands can enter tapped; red, the colour of Brallin and every wheel but three, sits furthest under its target. sharks-v1 swapped two lands: Thundering Falls (Island Mountain, enters tapped, surveil 1) for Talon Gates of Madara and Sundown Pass (R/W, untapped with two other lands) for Cascade Bluffs, so the phase-out land is gone. Smothering Tithe is filed here because Treasure is what it makes, and a symmetrical wheel is seven opponent draws per seat for it to tax; no passing stack has Tithe on the battlefield. Several lands do a second job, filed here because making mana is what they do every game: Command Beacon returns a commander to hand (a tax reset), Otawara bounces by channel, and Raugrin Triome and Glittering Massif cycle, which is a discard for Brallin (stack 003: a cost discard triggers him). Thundering Falls and Sundown Pass are among the lands stack 012's premise taps for the Shark Typhoon cycle: a legal mana pile, not a resolved step.

stages.label: A COMMANDER ON THE BATTLEFIELD
stages.what_it_does: The COMMANDER half of the engine does not pay until Shabraz (5 mana, flying) or Brallin (4 mana) has resolved and survived: without one a loot or a wheel grows no commander and Lae'zel, Bard and Teferi's Ageless Insight have no commander trigger to multiply, which is why the pilot holds wheels until a commander is out. It is not the whole engine: the second collectors pay with both commanders in the command zone, Razorkin Needlehead by stack 011 (a wheel under Torbran, 21 per seat) and Glint-Horn and Magmakin by oracle text (output). Shabraz turns each card drawn into a +1/+1 counter and 1 life; Brallin turns each card discarded into a +1/+1 counter and 1 damage to each opponent. The two hand each other evasion by oracle text: Brallin's {R} gives a Shark trample and Shabraz is a Shark Bird; Shabraz's {W/U} gives a Human flying and Brallin is a Human Shaman. The deck is modal: either one alone can be the 21-commander-damage threat, so the ignition is redundant, not single, and each removal adds 2 to that commander's tax. Both start in the command zone, so drawing them is never the constraint; casting and keeping them is. goldfish_metrics.json (10,000 games, the current decklist sha): Shabraz is cast by turn six in 88.3% (mean turn 4.909, median 5), Brallin in 95.6% (mean 4.005), and both are on the battlefield by turn six in 87.8%. The goldfish casts each once and has no removal, so these are a ceiling on the ignition, not its survival; the protection group is measured by turn six in 80.1% (deck-audit). goldfish_targets still calls a WHEEL 'the ignition' and marks it `required`; that reading is the one this model replaces (proposed_goldfish_edits[0]).

stages.label: EVERY CARD THAT MOVES
stages.what_it_does: Steady fuel between wheels: a loot pays both commanders at once (a draw for Shabraz, a discard for Brallin) without emptying the hand. Repeatable loots: Kitsa ({T}), Mary Read and Anne Bonny ({T}, plus a Treasure on a discarded Pirate or Island), Teferi, Master of Time (+1 at instant speed), Jeskai Ascendancy (per noncreature spell), Ledger Shredder (connive). One-shot loots: Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Sorcerer Class's entry, and Shark Typhoon's cycling, which is a discard and a draw at instant speed plus an X/X flying Shark (stack 012: Brallin, Mako and Shabraz each paid); on the battlefield it instead makes an X/X flying Shark per noncreature spell, by oracle text. Draw engines that tax opponents: Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Faerie Mastermind. Discard converters: Rielle draws as many as you discarded the first time each turn, and Inti discards on attack for a counter, trample and an impulse draw. Two narrow tutors aim the flow: Idyllic Tutor for an enchantment and Stoneforge Mystic for any of the four Equipment. The standing-draw group (eight cards) is in 45.6% of opening sevens and measured by turn six in 78.1%; the discard-converter group (Inti, Mako, Mary Read, Rielle, Shark Typhoon) in 31.2% and 64.4% (deck-audit). Kitsa is proven on boards of the 99 twice: stack 007 has its loot pay Brallin, stack 010 has it copy Wheel of Fortune. Stack 006 shows a loot between strikes making Shabraz 10 + 11 = 21, but its double strike was the cut Fireshrieker. There is no dedicated fodder stage: the deck eats its own hand.

stages.label: MAKE EACH CARD WORTH MORE
stages.what_it_does: The commanders convert one card into one counter or one ping; these nine raise what each card is worth. Counters: Lae'zel adds one to every counter placement (stack 008: Windfall gives Brallin 10 counters for 5 discards and Shabraz 14 for 7 draws). Draws: Bard, King of Dale and Teferi's Ageless Insight turn every draw into two except the first one in each of your draw steps, so a main-phase wheel's draws are all doubled; Consecrated Sphinx draws two per opponent draw, so a symmetrical wheel is 21 triggers (stack 009: 49 cards, Shabraz 52/52, and the cleanup discard of 42 fires Brallin past 40 at every seat). Knowledge Is Power makes the draw turn a pump turn for the whole team. Damage, on Brallin's pings and Razorkin Needlehead's: Torbran adds 2 per red-source event to an opponent (stack 005: Brallin's seven pings, 21 to each opponent; stack 011: Needlehead's seven, 21 each; neither a kill from 40), Artist's Talent at level 3 adds 2 per noncombat event (stack 004), and with Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation all out one ping is at least 8 per opponent, since each opponent orders the replacements (stack 007). The amplifier group (Torbran, Gratuitous Violence, Fiery Emancipation) is in 19.9% of opening sevens and measured by turn six in 45.6%; Lae'zel alone in 7.1% and 17.8% (deck-audit, which names it the deck's one single-card point of failure for its target). Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation also multiply commander combat damage by oracle text; no passing stack resolves combat under them.

stages.label: THE SECOND COLLECTORS
stages.what_it_does: What the engine produces besides a large commander: creatures that collect a second tax on the same cards. Glint-Horn Buccaneer deals 1 to each opponent per card discarded, a second Brallin (haste, and a {1}{R} loot while attacking). Magmakin Artillerist deals damage equal to the cards discarded to each opponent, once per discard event, and cycles. Marauding Mako grows a counter per card discarded and cycles. Razorkin Needlehead (sharks-v1, for Ghostly Pilferer) taxes the other half of a symmetrical wheel: 1 damage to an opponent per card that opponent draws, so Wheel of Fortune or Reforge the Soul is seven per seat on its own whatever your hand held (both draw seven; Brallin's, Glint-Horn's and Magmakin's halves are your discard count), and stack 011 resolves Wheel of Fortune under Needlehead and Torbran as seven triggers of 3 per opponent, 40 to 19, with no commander on the board. The declared second-damage group (Glint-Horn, Magmakin) is two cards: 13.7% of opening sevens, measured by turn six in 32.9% (deck-audit marks it thin); the wheel kill's damage component now names Needlehead as well, three cards in 19.9% of openers, and the paired wheel kill is measured by turn six in 33.9%. Stack 004 resolves Magmakin's blast for a seven-card discard as 7 to each opponent, 9 under Artist's Talent, beside Brallin's seven pings: 30 per seat. Stack 012 has Mako take a counter from a Shark Typhoon cycle. No passing stack has Glint-Horn on the battlefield, nor Needlehead beside Brallin.

stages.label: KEEP THE COMMANDER, CLEAR THE LANE
stages.what_it_does: The whole engine is one creature that a single removal spell answers. Constant cover: Lightning Greaves (haste and shroud, equip 0) and Robe of Stars (phase out). Held cover: Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat (free with a commander out), Loran's Escape, March of Swirling Mist, and the counters Negate, Stubborn Denial and Izzet Charm. Grand Abolisher shuts off responses on your own turn, which is the turn the wheel or the double-strike attack happens. Answers that clear a blocker or a hate piece: Swords to Plowshares, Get Lost, Chaos Warp, Prismari Command. The declared protection group (eight cards, counting Akroma's Will and Brotherhood Regalia, which this model files under wincon) is in 45.6% of opening sevens and measured by turn six in 80.1%; the answers group (nine) in 49.8% and 84.0% (deck-audit). sharks-v1 cut Boros Charm and Talon Gates of Madara, two of the deck's protective modes. The two group rates price DRAWING a card, never using it at the right moment. No passing stack resolves any of these protecting a commander from removal; stacks 005, 008 and 010 hold Negate, Swords or Lightning Greaves only as cards in hand or on the board.

stages.label: TWENTY-ONE, OR THE WHEEL
stages.what_it_does: Two endings, and the pilot chooses between them each game. COMMANDER DAMAGE: a grown commander connects for 21. The kit: double strike from Shu Yun (pay {R/W}{R/W} per noncreature spell), Embercleave, Blade Historian or Akroma's Will (which, with a commander out, also gives indestructible and protection from each colour); evasion from Brotherhood Regalia (can't be blocked, ward 2) or the commanders' own flying and trample grants. Stack 006 is the shape: a 10/10 double-striker that loots between strikes deals 10 + 11. Its double strike was the cut Fireshrieker, and sharks-v1 cut Boros Charm too, so none of the four double-strike sources now in the 99 has a passing stack: the kill is the deck's stated plan and an unproven line (open_questions[0]). THE WHEEL: a full-hand discard-and-draw with a commander out. Wheel of Fortune, Windfall, Reforge the Soul, Tolarian Winds (instant), Jace's Archivist (repeatable), Fateful Showdown (instant, plus damage equal to the hand), and the wheel modes of Collective Defiance and Incendiary Command. The wheel group is in 45.6% of opening sevens, drawn by turn three in 54.7% and measured by turn six in 73.1% (deck-audit), so the usual job is holding one, not finding one. A wheel pays one ping per card discarded: seven cards made 7 per seat (stack 001), a copied three-card hand 10 (stack 010), and under Consecrated Sphinx the cleanup discard is the kill (stack 009). Paired with a second per-card damage source (now including Needlehead) it is measured by turn six in 33.9%. A wheel also grows both commanders, so it feeds the first ending as well.

map_disagreements.why: The map files a wheel by the rest of its text: the five plain or near-plain wheels sit in Tutors, the two modal ones whose other modes deal damage (Collective Defiance, Incendiary Command) in Interaction, and Jace's Archivist, a creature with a tap ability, in Bodies. To the engine all eight are one finisher, because a discard pays Brallin and a draw pays Shabraz whatever else the card says.

Embercleave, Blade Historian and Brotherhood Regalia sit in the city now labelled Ramp beside the Equipment, enchantment multipliers and Signets; Akroma's Will reads as Interaction on its protective modes; Shu Yun sits with the commanders and loot creatures. All four do one job here: give a grown commander double strike or an unblocked lane. The voltron route is not visible in card text as a group.

The multipliers are replacement effects whose text names damage, counters or draws, and the map clusters on those nouns: the enchantments (Artist's Talent, Gratuitous Violence, Fiery Emancipation, Knowledge Is Power, Teferi's Ageless Insight) beside the Equipment, the creatures (Bard, Lae'zel, Torbran) with the commanders, Consecrated Sphinx with the draw engines. What unites them, multiplying a commander trigger, is a relation to Brallin and Shabraz that no single card's text states.

Loot creatures (Kitsa, Mary Read, Rielle, Inti) sit with the commanders; the draw engines and Shark Typhoon with Bodies; Faithless Looting, Frantic Search and Idyllic Tutor with the wheels in Tutors; Sorcerer Class and Teferi, Master of Time with the Equipment. They do one job here, paying both commanders at once.

Lightning Greaves, Robe of Stars and Grand Abolisher sit with the voltron Equipment, Chaos Warp in Tutors (it reveals off the top of a library); everything else that protects the window sits in Interaction.

The two Signets and Talisman of Creativity sit with the Equipment and enchantments, not with Sol Ring and Arcane Signet in Mana II. A reading, not a measurement: their activated two-colour text sits nearer that cluster than the colourless rocks do.

Glint-Horn, Magmakin and Mako cluster as creatures with Bodies; Razorkin Needlehead, the draw-side collector, lands with the enchantment amplifiers it pairs with (Torbran's +2, stack 011). To the engine all four are one job, a second tax on a wheel's cards; the declared wheel-kill damage group shows the same split (Bodies 2, Ramp 1).

Against deck_map.json at 7bbc74bf (v2.1.1), the v2.2.0 map changed the label on every one of its seven city ids (0 Card Flow->Ramp, 1 Finishers->Bodies, 2 Interaction->Mana, 3 Mana->Interaction, 4 Ramp->Mana II, 5 Tutors->Card Flow, 6 Bodies->Tutors). Matched by membership, Mana, Interaction and Tutors kept their labels under new ids; the old Ramp cluster kept city-4 and is now Mana II (9 of 9 members); the old Finishers cluster is now Ramp (10 of 17); and the old Card Flow and Bodies clusters swapped labels (11 of 12, 10 of 10). That is why three labels no longer describe their members: 'Ramp' (city-0) holds Embercleave, Lightning Greaves and three damage enchantments beside three mana rocks, 'Card Flow' (city-5) holds both commanders, Torbran and Shu Yun, and 'Bodies' (city-1) holds Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora and Jeskai Ascendancy. This model cites the labels as the map prints them; the mismatch is a finding about the labeller, not the deck.
